reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that thermal aging can produce coherent nanoprecipitates in a W-based refractory HEA and that these improve mechanical properties, but it provides no data on irradiation response, defect dynamics, or radiation tolerance. The key premises about radiation-induced defect mitigation and mechanical integrity under irradiation are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Thermal aging of a W-based refractory HEA can induce coherent nanoprecipitates
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as defect sinks and modify defect migration pathways
Modified defect migration enhances point-defect recombination and suppresses void swelling
The nanoprecipitate-modified alloy retains mechanical integrity (strength and ductility)
The effect holds under fusion-relevant irradiation conditions (~100 dpa)
